text:
alex: Heads up — after yesterday's batching tweak I noticed a ~15% p95 latency regression on the reranker/embeddings non-chat endpoints. (/v1/emb/ and /v1/rerank). Numbers came from Canary-232 across eu-west-1.

maria: Ugh. Was that the change that increased the continuous batching window to 8ms? I remember we bumped it to reduce tiny batch overhead.

alex: Yep, we moved from 4ms -> 8ms and increased max_batch_tokens from 2048 -> 4096 for a longer time-slice. The interesting bit: regression mostly for short queries (1-8 tokens).

jing: That matches what I'd expect — extended window makes single-token embedding requests sit in the queue waiting for more requests, creating head-of-line queuing and larger micro-batches that flip kernel selection heuristics. For seq_len=1 we sometimes hit the generic matmul kernel instead of the optimized small-seq path.

sam: Can you paste a profile? CPU/GPU kernel timeline ideally. Also want to know if KV cache touches the path (shouldn't for embeddings).

alex: Profiling snippets below from debug-run on canary2 (trimmed):
```
[profiling] timeline: queue_wait 7.9ms -> batch_build 1.2ms -> forward 12.4ms -> postprocess 0.8ms
[kernel] matmul_generic: 9.2ms (hot)
[kernel] small_seq_attention_fast: 0.6ms (cold)
[batch] size distribution: 1: 48%, 2: 22%, 4+: 30%
```

maria: That matmul_generic time is the smoking gun. When small batches with seq_len=1/2 get aggregated into larger token-budget batches they change the kernel selection codepath which can be worse on A1008 configs for this layer ordering.

jing: Two knobs to consider: 1) route embeddings/rerank to a separate queue with lower max_wait_ms and token_budget_target tuned to keep batch token counts small; 2) adjust kernel selection thresholds so small-seq optimized kernels are preferred for sequences <= 4 even if overall batch token count is higher. Option #1 is lower risk.

alex: I ran a quick sim toggling token_budget_target from 4096 -> 512 for the embeddings queue. Sim throughput drops ~3% but p95 improves ~18% for short queries. Seems like a good trade for customer-facing rerank endpoints.

sam: Agree. We should also add an inline metric for `kernel_choice` per-inference so we can break down percent of requests hitting generic vs optimized kernels. Then can monitor after rollout.

devon: Product note — a small throughput hit is fine if latency is predictable. We have latency SLOs for the hosted embeddings SLA; this seems aligned. Just confirm cost impact.

alex: Cost delta on projected 100k qps: +2.5% GPU time. Will quantify in PR.

maria: Action plan:
- Create a per-route queue policy for `*/v1/emb*` and `*/v1/rerank*` with max_wait_ms=4 and token_budget_target=512.
- Add metric `model.kernel_choice` (labels: optimized|generic) and exposure in Console.
- Add a canary in eu-west-1 on Dedicated and run soak for 6h.

sam: Also: add a temporary feature-flag to revert to global queue behavior quickly. If canary shows throughput collapse we can flip it.

alex: I'll open the PR and attach perf runs. PR will include the queue policy JSON and the small change to the kernel-selection table that pins small-seq kernels for seq_len<=2 behind a flag.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary job scheduled: canary-deploy/emb-queue-tune -> eu-west-1 on hostpool-dedicated-3. ETA 10min. :rocket:

jing: One more note — check KV cache warms: even though embeddings don't use KV, reranker sometimes runs same model variant as chat and code path shares KV cache init. If canary nodes have cold KV, initial latency spike possible. Warm the cache with background priming requests.

alex: Good call. I'll add a priming job: 2k synthetic short embeddings at t0 on the canary hosts.

devon: Great. Let's reconvene after 6h soak or earlier if metrics spike. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
